title: CLO X Coach Contest
content:
Dear CLO Team,

I’m interested in the CLO X Coach Contest and have a few questions regarding the requirements:

  1. Regarding the line:  
_"Judges would like to see your concept, research/process work, and a file rendering of your leather goods capsule inclusive of handbag(s), bag charm(s), and lifestyle objects."_  
Does this mean that we should document the entire 3D design process — for example, by including concept sketches, screenshots from CLO, or a short presentation showing our workflow?

  2. Is having a personal CLO3D license a requirement for participating in the contest?

Thank you in advance for your help!![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202507/8c2baa90ba1d4dd497ac5f1300003ce8/images/f84a5b04a7e14e4492e6d9cbd01cc13dcov.png)





### Community Post Comments:
Comment 1: Hi Ariel, To create a beautiful and detailed model, high-resolution materials are often necessary. I've had multiple cases where the project file exceeded the 500 MB limit. What are the recommended ways to reduce the file size to meet the requirements?Is it allowed to use materials with the lowest possible resolution during submission, even if they are not the same resolution as those used in the final render? Would that be acceptable?Also, I have another question: is it permitted to use minimal AI assistance in the final renders?Thanks!Mel

Comment 2: Hi Ariel,Thanks for your earlier reply! I just want to confirm a few more details about the submission format, as I’ve seen some others had similar questions too:1) Can research content and design process (like a portfolio-style layout) be submitted as a PDF, or only as image files (JPEG/PNG)?2) If PDFs are allowed, is there a file size limit or page count limit?3) Is the 1–3 image limit meant only for final renders, or does that include any research images too?4) Lastly, is there a total number or size limit for all files we can upload?Just want to make sure I’m submitting things properly and not exceeding any limits - face uploading errors. Thanks again for your help!

Comment 3: Hi There!1) You can choose what/how much you would like to share. Any of the options mentioned above are great2) A Valid personal CLO License should be used
Reply 1: Thank you!
Reply 2: Hi there, just an addition on this subject, Submission Guidelines mention: 1 Project File (.zprj) No larger than 500 MB1-3 Final Renders (.png or .jpeg) Max Image resolution of 4KMax Image file size of 10MBProject File & Renders must include at least 1 handbagIncluding additional items of your choice, such as bag charms, garments, avatars, etc is Optional.If we would like to upload a research file , where would that be?
Reply 3: Hi AntoniaK. Research files would also be uploaded as part of the submission. Same place renders would be
content_description: This page serves as a resource for participants of the CLO X Coach Contest to clarify requirements and seek guidance on the submission process.

title: CONNECT upload issues, which file formats are supported by thumbnails when the store uploads files？
content:
CONNECT upload issues, what file formats does the thumbnail support when the store uploads a file?  
I flipped through the reference manual:  
Supported image formats: jpeg/.png/.bmp, supported video formats: webp, videos in non-WEBP formats such as MP4, AVI, etc. must be converted to WEBP format and uploaded as thumbnails.  
Why can't I upload thumbnails when I convert video format to WEBP format?  
Can I only upload jpeg/.png/.bmp?  
Can I upload only attached images in WEBP format?  
The last time I uploaded the attached image to the file, I added an image in WEBP format, but the attached image could not be seen after the upload was successful.  
I now have a question about whether thumbnails can be used above transmission diagrams, and what formats are supported?![984edb8db639462aa74cdc203a3dca82](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202507/9eae1e2cde2d45c29f690f5a7ff0545e/images/984edb8db639462aa74cdc203a3dca82675aef31082482f3e6134c70dadec81e.png)![adf14aacb52e4a1a8391e6eb99985ad0](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202507/9eae1e2cde2d45c29f690f5a7ff0545e/images/adf14aacb52e4a1a8391e6eb99985ad0dde18e76b9db50daf0ba04dd6056d177.png)


### Community Post Comments:
Comment 1: Hi, CLO footageWe limit thumbnail uploads to JPG and PNG only, in order to ensure a seamless browsing experience for users when viewing items. Since loading speed is less critical when opening an item's detail page, WebP animation can be used for additional images.When using WebP animation, it is limited to a total of 50 megapixels (the sum of sizes of all frames). This is a guideline of the image delivery service used on our platform. If this limit is exceeded, the WebP image may not be displayed properly.
Reply 1: Okay, thanks for the answer, the reference manual can explain it properly or mark the thumbnail with JPG and PNG upload only
content_description: This page provides essential information on supported file formats for thumbnails during uploads, troubleshooting common issues, and clarifying the use of WEBP images.

Every time she wore it, it felt like reclaiming a part of herself — strong, warm, and ready to face a new path.

It wasn’t just a jacket.  
It was a quiet companion — in the wind, in the stillness, in the memory.

title: Creating Nails in CLO3D – No Extra Software Needed
content:
![bbf80d9a2a814a3f8a4de67e6a77fb9b](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202507/c9633dd4f90a460e94ace3a5f339702e/images/bbf80d9a2a814a3f8a4de67e6a77fb9bUntitled%20design-7.png)

Whenever I post an outfit or create final renders for personal projects or clients, I like to go the extra mile - not only finishing the clothes down to the last detail, but also adding accessories like **nails** 💅.

The odd thing? There are only a few nail assets in the CLO library.

The good thing? It’s surprisingly easy to make your own! ✨

* * *

# **For a simple manicure:**

  1. Download the **arm folding image** file

  2. Paint the nails in your chosen color

  3. Export as **PNG**

  4. Replace the original arm folding image with your new one




# **For a more detailed nail set:**

  1. Create the nail base using a small curved pattern (like you’d make a rigid trim)

  2. Shape and scale it to match the avatar’s nail bed

  3. Use **pins** and **internal lines** to position and curve it around the finger

  4. Apply **thickness** and **texture** to simulate polish, gloss, or nail art

  5. Freeze to avoid deformation during simulation




* * *

By creating nails this way, you can manually place and pose them on the avatar.

But keep in mind: **adding the nails should be the very last step before rendering** , since fabric-based nails do **not follow** avatar poses.

# **Why not convert them into accessories?**

I’ve tried that - but here’s the limitation:

CLO accessories can’t be rigged to individual fingers. So the nails stay locked in place, not following hand or finger movement. That’s why I recommend leaving them as fabric-based nails. It’s the most flexible solution!

Have you tried making nails yourself? Or found another hack to do it faster? 👀

By the way - this is a render of my most recent nail asset! It’s now available for purchase on my profile. Go check it out! 💥


### Community Post Comments:
Comment 1: Great tip! Thank you. I will try to do my own nails 💅
Reply 1: Do it! Add some internal lines in the middle to make them slightly curved😉
content_description: Discover how to create custom nail designs for your CLO projects, enhancing your outfits with personalized details that truly stand out!

title: Why is my render in low quality even though Im using a good PC, NVIDIA graphics and nice set-ups?
content:
I spent 30 min rendering this image but as you can see it below, it turn out like crap. What am I doing wrong? Im so tired, what dont know what else to do. Do I need to wait for the render preview to load completely? And if I do, why does it keep stuck for half a hour in the same spot?

![8ab6a332721c452ea461818e137d69a9](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202507/1a2af4aabf70474ba4ee144739f0580f/images/8ab6a332721c452ea461818e137d69a9Screenshot%202025-07-07%20152210.png)![5adf0e95a6ef4517a111076334cac5f5](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202507/1a2af4aabf70474ba4ee144739f0580f/images/5adf0e95a6ef4517a111076334cac5f5render2.jpg)![61a29081c912486b86ab87cdd8cd7b79](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202507/1a2af4aabf70474ba4ee144739f0580f/images/61a29081c912486b86ab87cdd8cd7b79Screenshot%202025-07-07%20152255.png)![223b5a91fabc4a0b9660ded38f899404](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202507/1a2af4aabf70474ba4ee144739f0580f/images/223b5a91fabc4a0b9660ded38f899404Screenshot%202025-07-07%20152409.png)![31e6466adad04064badcc025cacd77cd](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202507/1a2af4aabf70474ba4ee144739f0580f/images/31e6466adad04064badcc025cacd77cdScreenshot%202025-07-07%20152237.png)


### Community Post Comments:
Comment 1: Looks amazing and like you have it all sorted out...I just thought even the first image looked high quality, just blurred. My thought was to uncheck Depth of Field.

Comment 2: A few other pointersNoise : 0.030 is the lowest we recommend. The human eye will not see the difference and reducing to 0.010 will just increase the time it takesQuality for both Material & Light. This is about how light bounces in a scene. Unless you are building scenes with walls/furniture where light has places to bounce. Keeping it at Medium is usually ok. Since the dress it metallic I would maybe increase material to High

Comment 3: Did you click the second button or the first? In the photo I circled the right button to left click. The first one does not do the render. When the render is done a popup window will appear and will lead you to the folder where your render image was saved.

Comment 4: Hi, did you use "focus by left click" by any chance under Depth of Field? Could you tick off Physical Camera completely and try again? (On a general note, please see this article: https://connect.clo-set.com/community/post/1a2af4aabf70474ba4ee144739f0580f
Reply 1: hi! it does look better, but that is so weird.... my teacher in CLO3D at uni told me to put exact this values and in his file it worked...
Reply 2: this was our first try together, with exact the same parameters and it worked!
Reply 3: Hi Barbara, the focus by left click can produce blurry results based on where you left-click on the image. I like to use it to get a more "photographed"-looking output, but you just have to play with it a bit and see what result you like. It is best to use it and click after you've already decided on the angle and cutout you want. It will be taken into account by the interactive render, so you can have it load a bit and see if you really want to render this output before you do. Hope this helps!
content_description: This web page aims to seek advice and troubleshooting tips for improving rendering quality and addressing performance issues in 3D rendering software.
